events.title: Challenger is lost
events.description: Seven people die when the shuttle breaks apart after launch. NASA pauses shuttle flights and investigates.

events.title: A speech at the Berlin Wall
events.description: President Reagan calls for the wall to be opened and removed. The wall remains in place at this point.

events.title: Black Monday shakes markets
events.description: The Dow falls 22.6% in one day. Your chart shows monthly returns, so its October drop is a different number.

what_happened_next.text:
Computers were exciting at the start, but the international share basket finished well ahead of Apple and IBM. Disney also rose strongly. Over these five years, $10,000 in the international basket became about $42,200, compared with about $11,900 in IBM. A famous growth industry did not guarantee the strongest return.

Apple released the Macintosh in 1984 and IBM introduced a new PS/2 computer family in 1987. Disney’s first Touchstone movie, Splash, came out in 1984 as the studio tried to reach older audiences. Each company relied on different products and customers. Their stories help describe the businesses, but do not explain the full share returns.

October 1987 brought Black Monday. The Dow fell 22.6% in a day. The monthly chart combines that terrible day with the rest of October, so it shows a different number. All seven choices nevertheless ended higher over the full five years.

This result does not prove foreign shares always win. It shows that familiar companies are only part of the investment world. What you pay, what happens next and when you measure the result all matter.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The recovery and new technology competed for attention with elections, jobs and cultural events. Apple and IBM were easy companies to notice.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The price paid for an investment mattered alongside its story. A broad basket outside the US beat these famous computer companies over this particular window.
reflection.what_faded_away: Excitement about a movie or a new computer could not settle a five-year investing decision. An interesting headline was only a small piece of information.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: No one knew the date of the coming crash or the final ranking. Spreading money across companies reduced reliance on one business, but it did not prevent market-wide falls.

hot:1983-05:apple.text: Apple introduced the Macintosh in January 1984, giving customers a personal computer with pictures and menus they controlled using a mouse. The Mac gave Apple a new kind of computer to sell; Apple shares ended higher over this five-year window.

hot:1983-05:ibm.text: IBM announced its PS/2 line in April 1987 and reported more than one million sold by November. Those sales showed buyers were taking up the new computer family; IBM shares ended higher during this window.

hot:1983-05:disney.text: On March 9, 1984, Disney released Splash as the first Touchstone film, using a new label for movies aimed at older audiences. Touchstone widened Disney’s movie business beyond family animation; Disney shares rose over five years.
